title: Development and evaluation of a nationwide "quality network for returning to work after cancer" in outpatient cancer counselling centres
summary:
In Germany, 35% of new cancer cases affect people of working age. Staying in and returning to work with or after the disease often leads to challenges for those affected.
Cancer counselling centres (KBS) provide patients and their relatives with access to psychosocial counselling in all phases of the disease. Professional reintegration can be part of the counselling process. Whether CABs provide comprehensive counselling on this topic depends, among other things, on the knowledge of the counsellors.
As part of the previous CARES project, counsellors from the cancer counselling centres were trained as career guides whose task it is to advise those seeking advice more intensively on returning to work.
The aim of the subsequent QV-CARES project is to consolidate the intensified and needs-oriented return-to-work counselling developed during the CARES study in cancer counselling centres.
The focus of the study is to continuously evaluate the programme in the sense of accompanying care research.
The existing curriculum for the training programme for career guides will be expanded on the basis of quantitative and qualitative data collected in the CARES study, requirements for career guides in CABs will be formulated and an online tool for long-term data collection will be introduced. At the end of the project, a permanent quality development structure for vocational reintegration and continuous data collection will be implemented.

interventions.name: People seeking advice from cancer counselling centres with work-related questions: Inclusion of advice seekers of working age who have received intensified counselling at a cancer counselling centre as part of the career guidance programme. No comparison group.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Counselling at a cancer counselling centre as part of the career guidance programme (Berufslots*innen)
Exclusion criteria:
Cognitive and/or physical limitations that prevent participation in the online survey, lack of German language skills
